limits: No experiment of the chapter's own: all results are relayed from cited papers, none with metrics.
The travel planner is a toy on static data with GPT-2; no evaluation is reported.
The chapter states LLMs cannot yet automate complex business needs and need human oversight.
HuggingGPT limits named: efficiency (3 of 4 steps call the LLM), planning quality, context length, instability.
Virtual Lab limits named: training cutoff, hand-crafted agenda and prompts, needs human guidance, drifts off task.
Agent Laboratory limits named: weak novelty, code bugs, high cost, imperfect agent communication.
Business-model section has no data; Table 9.1 is qualitative.
practices: Describe each model/tool in text and put the descriptions in the prompt, so new tools need no training (HuggingGPT).
When descriptions exceed context, filter by task type and rank, then give the LLM only top-k (Model selection).
Use a <resource> placeholder to carry dependencies between tasks and run independent tasks in parallel (Model execution).
Use an external tool for arithmetic instead of the LLM (travel planner calculate_total_price).
Build judge ensembles from different models, not copies of one (multi-agent for law).
Keep a human in the loop for creativity and judgment in research agents (Virtual Lab, Agent Laboratory).
Add RAG or search so agents know tools newer than the training cutoff (Virtual Lab limits).
Combine LLM bulk labelling with human validation for agent fine-tuning data (Agent strategies).
Pick the business model (SaaS/MaaS/DaaS/RaaS) before development because costs do not allow trial and error (Business models).
